edge_cases: Missing or empty form fields cause a server error (no explicit validation).
Database connection failures or query errors result in an unhandled exception.
SQL injection is possible because user input is concatenated directly into SQL statements.
Very long input values may exceed database column limits and cause insertion failures.
If random session_id generation fails, the session creation step will error.
If the redirect URL parameters exceed URL length limits, the client may reject the response.
contract.intent: Create a new user account and start a session for the user if the chosen username is not already taken.
invariants: A username must be unique; duplicate usernames are rejected.
The password is always stored as a bcrypt hash, never in plain text.
All required form fields (username, password, name, email, cweid) must be present for successful registration.
A session record is created only after the user record is successfully inserted.
io_behavior: Accepts an HTTP POST request to /register with form fields: username, password, name, email, cweid.
If registration succeeds, responds with an HTTP redirect to /login including username, session_id, and stake as query parameters.
If the username already exists, responds with a plain‑text message "Username is already taken".
side_effects: Inserts a new row into the users table with the supplied data and a bcrypt‑hashed password.
Inserts a new row into the sessions table containing a generated session_id linked to the new user.
Commits the above inserts to the MySQL database.

rationale: The program fulfills core registration flow and unique‑username check, hashes passwords, and redirects on success, but it adds explicit missing‑field handling (instead of a server error), prevents SQL injection, and fails to insert a session record, breaking several contract edge‑cases and side‑effects.
